summary.title: On being an Engineering Manager
summary.one_liner: A solutions architect's six-month personal review of acting as an Engineering Manager, covering the new people-management duties, the calendar load of 1-on-1s, and why he chose to return to the technical track.
takeaways: Going from architect to people manager brings new duties such as performance management, leave and expense approval, timesheets, budgeting and hiring.
Fortnightly one-on-ones with a whole team consume large amounts of calendar time; the author suggests shortening them when needed and holding them outside the meeting room.
Technical leaders already practise a lot of leadership (influence, communication, empathy), so those soft skills matter on either track.
Choosing between the management and technical tracks depends on what you enjoy and where the organisation needs you; the author chose to stay technical as a solution architect.
summary.summary: This is a first-person reflection published in February 2019, written after about six months acting as an Engineering Manager in a large organisation. The author describes why he took the role, the new processes he had to learn (1-on-1s, appraisals, hiring, budgeting, timesheets) and how his calendar changed. He explains why he then decided not to apply for the permanent post and to stay on the technical side as a solution designer or architect. The post is informal and experience-based, with no code or formal method, and it closes with practical tips and lessons on soft skills and technical leadership.
